newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: EUROPEAN FEEDS TRADE FOCUSES ON U.S. DATA.
newsitem.headline: EUROPEAN FEEDS TRADE FOCUSES ON U.S. DATA.

text.p: Key U.S. crop data due on Tuesday is the main focus for Europe's meals and feeds trade this week amid cash markets subdued by new harvests.
Analysts have said they expect the report to show a record 1997/98 soybean crop, but some reckoned the estimate would be below the 2.69 billion bushel figure released in July.
Europe-based analyst Arie van Dijk of Stigevo said he expected a bearish figure from the USDA which, if accompanied by reports of rain in key growing areas, could spark a sell-off.
He said CBOT November soybeans could dip below six dollars from a close on Friday of $6.37-1/2.
But an additional factor this year was the average yield.

"The USDA is talking about 38.5 bushels an acre but others up to 39.5 bushels," he said. "With 15 percent of acreage devoted to genetically modified beans, the yields are going to be bigger than normal."
The weather was the other problem for the European trade, with compounder buying limited to absolute necessities.
"We've seen this weather game every July and August for years and we still have no clue how to cope with it. The only thing we can do it to sit back and wait until the crop is in," one broker said.
The slight weakening of the dollar against the guilder and the mark might encourage buying, but traders said the rate was still prohibitively high.
Van Dijk said he was maintaining his advice to clients to buy any weather dips to cover short-term needs, but to hold off from covering November through to April until September.
"I have a feeling the ending stocks figure could be better than expected, so my advice is to wait," he said.

In other products, pressure on local markets from the rapeseed harvest continued to be felt, accentuated by reports that Poland's crop would be better than expected. There were also reports of high stocks of rape meal in Germany, Van Dijk said.
He estimated a good European crop at 8.3 million tonnes.
On Monday, France's oilseeds association SIDO revised its rapeseed crop estimate up by 120,000 tonnes, pegging the harvest at a record of more than three million tonnes this year.
Relatively low prices for beet pulp and citrus pulp might encourage buying from feed compounders this week, he added.
